title: qsort and Comparators
concept: qsort provides general-purpose sorting of arrays of various types with a void pointer and comparison callback.

steps.title: Include required headers
steps.explanation: `stdio.h` provides the output, and `stdlib.h` provides the `qsort` declaration.

steps.title: Definition of comparison function (Comparator)
steps.explanation:
`compare(const void*, const void*)` is the comparison callback signature required by qsort.

The return sign determines the sort order.

steps.title: Value Extraction (Casting & Dereferencing)
steps.explanation:
Cast `void*` to the actual type (`int*`) and then dereference it to read the value.

If the types do not match, you will get incorrect results.

steps.title: Return comparison result
steps.explanation: Returns negative/0/positive to pass the preceding/equal/following order to qsort.

steps.title: main function and array declaration
steps.explanation: Prepare the array to be sorted and the number of elements.

steps.title: qsort call
steps.explanation:
Sort an array in-place with `qsort(arr, n, sizeof(int), compare)`.

Sorting criteria logic is provided by the compare function.
steps.keyInsight: qsort receives sorting criteria externally through comparison functions.

steps.title: Sort result output
steps.explanation: After sorting, print the array values ​​and check the results.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Exit with `return 0;`.

Bottom line: qsort's flexibility comes from its comparison callbacks.

quiz.question: How does qsort behave if its comparison function returns a positive number (+)?
options: It is determined that the first element (a) is greater than the second element (b), so its position is changed in ascending order.
It is judged that the two elements are equal.
quiz.explanation: In ascending sorting, if a - b is a positive number, a > b, so a must be sent backwards (swap).

misconceptions.wrong: Comparison function parameters can be declared as `int a, int b`.
misconceptions.correct:
No.
It must be a pointer of type `const void *a`, and the value must be read internally.
misconceptions.why: This is because qsort passes the 'address of the value' rather than the value itself.

keyTakeaway: Writing comparison functions using void* casting is a core pattern in C language generic programming.
